Venus, Mesa's Vulkan driver for virtio-gpu (src/virtio/vulkan), and
virgl, its OpenGL one (src/gallium/drivers/virgl, through Mesa's WGL
opengl32), from Mesa 26.2.4 (https://mesa3d.org/), used under the MIT
licence.  Not vendored whole: tools/build_venus.py fetches the release
tarball (checking its SHA-256), applies novaos.patch, adds
vn_renderer_nova.c and virgl_nova_winsys.c and builds vulkan_virtio.dll,
opengl32.dll (shipped as opengl32_virgl.dll) and libgallium_virgl.dll,
64- and 32-bit, with MinGW-w64.  The result, venus.7z, is the App Store's
"Venus" (the CI publishes it beside nova.iso).

vn_renderer_nova.c (MIT, NovaOS's own): Venus's renderer back end for
NovaOS, in place of Linux's virtgpu (DRM) and vtest ones.  It asks the
kernel's virtio-gpu driver (kernel/drivers/virtio_gpu.c, through
kernel/um/um_gpu.c's NtNovaGpuCtl, found in ntdll) for a 3D context on the
Venus capability set, submits Venus's command streams, creates and maps
blobs (a mappable one comes back as a section that NtMapViewOfSection
maps) and uses the kernel's timelines for Vulkan's timeline semaphores and
fences.  It also stubs three SPIR-V specialization helpers the Windows
link wants but Venus never calls.

virgl_nova_winsys.c (MIT; follows Mesa's virgl_vtest_winsys.c, Red Hat,
MIT): virgl's winsys for NovaOS, in place of Linux's DRM and vtest ones.
It opens a 3D context on the VIRGL2 capability set, creates classic 3D
resources with guest pages (mapped as sections) or, for persistent and
coherent maps, host blobs, sends command streams and transfers, each
fenced on one timeline the context numbers in submission order, and
shows frames through the WGL display target (gdi_sw_winsys) after reading
the front buffer back.

novaos.patch changes:
- src/virtio/vulkan/meson.build: build vn_renderer_nova.c on Windows.
- src/virtio/vulkan/vn_renderer.h: vn_renderer_create() makes the NovaOS
  renderer on Windows.
- src/virtio/vulkan/vn_instance.c: VK_KHR_win32_surface (Venus's
  Windows build left it out; DXVK needs it).
- src/virtio/vulkan/vn_common.h: no sync files on Windows (sync_wait and
  sync_valid_fd say every fd is signaled; ETIME defined).
- src/vulkan/runtime/vk_instance.c: with VK_ICD_PRESENT_HOOK defined,
  vk_icdNegotiateLoaderICDInterfaceVersion asks that function whether the
  device is there and declines otherwise, so the Vulkan loader moves on
  to the next driver (lavapipe) on a machine without a 3D virtio-gpu.
- src/vulkan/wsi/wsi_common_win32.cpp: MinGW-w64's d3d12.h instead of the
  DirectX-Headers project's (the DXGI swap chain path is not used; images
  are presented through GDI), and a present on a GPU's CPU image waits for
  the copy into it to finish (Mesa waits only on a software device).

- src/gallium/meson.build, src/gallium/drivers/virgl/meson.build and the
  new src/gallium/winsys/virgl/nova/ (meson.build, virgl_nova_public.h):
  build virgl_nova_winsys.c into virgl on Windows.
- src/gallium/targets/wgl/wgl.c and meson.build: the WGL target tries
  virgl first (GALLIUM_DRIVER=virgl, or the default when the GPU is
  there) and presents through the screen's flush_frontbuffer.

The 32-bit build links with --add-stdcall-alias, so the vk_icd*, gl* and
wgl* exports also have names without the stdcall @N suffix (Mesa's own
.def files do that for its other drivers; --kill-at would strip the @N
names opengl32 links against in libgallium_virgl's import library).
